item.title: The geopolitics of climate: Where next for climate progress after COP31?
item.description:
The geopolitics of climate: Where next for climate progress after COP31? 3 December 2026 — 12:30 TO 13:30 GMT Anonymous (not verified) 26 November 2026 Online

Hear from experts on what progress can be made after COP31.

Hear from experts on what progress can be made after COP31.

COP31 ended without an overarching deal after the longest UN climate talks on record. Disputes over fossil fuels and climate finance exposed deep geopolitical divisions. With agreement between major emitters harder to secure, where can progress now come from, and what roles could Europe, China and the United Kingdom play?

This event discusses:

  • What does COP31’s collapse mean for global climate action?
  • Is geopolitical rivalry now a greater obstacle than disagreement over climate policy?
  • How have conflict, energy prices and US politics disrupted progress? Will the mid-term results begin to shift the US stance?
  • Can Europe and China cooperate on climate even as trade tensions grow?
  • Where can governments rebuild momentum on fossil fuels and climate finance?
  • What can the United Kingdom achieve through its G20 and G7 presidencies?

item.title: Israel kills nine in Gaza, including a Hamas-appointed minister, officials say
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi

CAIRO, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Israeli airstrikes and gunfire killed at least nine Palestinians in Gaza overnight, medics said, including the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education, in a third consecutive night of air attacks despite a one-year-oldceasefire.

Medics said an Israeli airstrike hit an apartment in Deir Al-Balah, in central Gaza Strip on Thursday, killing Khaled Abu Nada, the deputy Gaza education minister, and his wife.

item.title: Pakistan, Saudi, Turkey to hold Mecca alliance meeting in Islamabad Nov 27-28, sources say
item.description:
ISLAMABAD, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey will hold a meeting on their mutual defence agreement in Islamabad this week, two Pakistani sources said on Thursday.

Foreign ministers of Saudi Arabia and Turkey are arriving in Pakistan to attend the meeting, which will be held on Friday and Saturday, the sources told Reuters.

The three countries signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca in August amid escalating concerns about the increasingly aggressive US-Israeli war against Iran.

Istanbul club Besiktas' supporters unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during a UEFA Europa League match against Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva in Georgia on Thursday, prompting a police response and sparking a diplomatic incident that led Turkey's foreign minister to contact his Georgian counterpart.

Turkish football fans clashed with police in Batumi, temporarily halting the match, which had been moved from Istanbul over security concerns.

item.title: Settlers smash foundations of Palestinian family's homes in West Bank
item.description:
By Pesha Magid

JALOUD, West Bank, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Militant Israeli settlers smashed the foundations of two homes belonging to a Palestinian family in the West Bank on Thursday, after settler attacks prevented the family from returning to them in defiance of an Israeli court order.

Security cameras showed the settlers bringing a bulldozer to the hilltop two-storey houses on either side of a road in the village of Jaloud at around 1 a.m. and spending about an hour damaging the houses. The family said it had been forced out months ago.

item.title: Co-leader of Germany's AfD criticises planned talks with Russian envoy
item.description:
By John O'Donnell

BERLIN, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Alternative for Germany co-leader Alice Weidel has criticised an AfD lawmaker's plans to meet a Kremlin envoy, dealing a blow to Moscow's efforts to woo the opposition far-right party as Russia tries to build support for resuming gas deliveries to Europe.

Bundestag member Markus Frohnmaier is preparing to attend talks in Abu Dhabi in February or March with Kirill Dmitriev, President Vladimir Putin's top business envoy, to discuss trade, including restarting gas supplies to Germany.

item.title: Hamas weighs response after Israel kills 10 people in Gaza
item.description:
By Nidal al-Mughrabi

CAIRO, Nov 26 (Reuters) - Hamas chief Khalil Al-Hayya said on Thursday the group was not prepared to withstand continued Israeli attacks, after local medics said Israeli strikes killed at least 10 people in Gaza, including the Hamas-appointed deputy minister of education.

Hayya's statement was a rare sign of possible retaliation since Israel has stepped up attacks against the group in recent months, killing dozens of leaders and members.
